subject: Chemistry
description: Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs — properties, trends, reactions, biological role

questions.stem: The ALKALI METALS belong to which group of the periodic table?

options.option_text: Group 2, the alkaline earth metals like Mg, Ca
Group 1 (excluding hydrogen), Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr
Group 17, the halogens like F, Cl, Br, I
Group 18, the noble gases like He, Ne, Ar

questions.explanation: ALKALI METALS — Group 1 (formerly IA): Lithium, Sodium, Potassium, Rubidium, Caesium, Francium. (Hydrogen sits in Group 1 by electron configuration but is NOT classified as an alkali metal.) Single valence electron → eager to lose it → form +1 cations. Highly reactive — must be stored under oil to prevent reaction with air/moisture. Distractor 1 = Group 2 alkaline earth metals (Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, Ra). Distractor 3 = halogens. Distractor 4 = noble gases.

questions.stem: Alkali metals are stored under KEROSENE OIL because they:

options.option_text: Float on top of kerosene for easy retrieval
React vigorously with both air and moisture
Smell pleasant when sealed under kerosene
Become much harder if stored long under it

questions.explanation: Alkali metals are EXTREMELY REACTIVE — react with O₂ in air (forming oxides), water vapour (forming hydroxides + H₂ which can ignite). Storing under kerosene (water-free, hydrophobic, non-reactive) excludes both. Lithium can also be stored under petroleum jelly. Sodium and potassium especially dangerous — react explosively with water. Distractor 1 — sodium is denser than kerosene, sinks. Distractors 3, 4 — irrelevant.

questions.stem: Down the alkali metal group from Li to Cs, REACTIVITY toward water:

options.option_text: Decreases gradually as we move downward
Increases dramatically (Cs reacts explosively)
Stays exactly the same for every alkali metal
Has no clear pattern from element to element

questions.explanation: Alkali metals + water → alkali hydroxide + H₂. Reactivity: Li (slow fizz) < Na (vigorous, may catch fire) < K (ignites instantly) < Rb (explodes) < Cs (explodes more violently). Reason: ionisation energy DECREASES down the group → outer e⁻ more easily lost → more reactive. Compare halogens — opposite trend (reactivity decreases down).

questions.stem: When sodium reacts with chlorine gas, the product is:

options.option_text: Sodium hydroxide, a strong base solution
Sodium chloride, common salt with ionic structure
Sodium chlorate, used in matches industry
Sodium hypochlorite, used in bleach products

questions.explanation: 2 Na + Cl₂ → 2 NaCl. Vigorous reaction with bright yellow flame. Sodium loses 1 e⁻ (Na → Na⁺); chlorine gains 1 e⁻ (Cl₂ + 2e⁻ → 2Cl⁻). Forms ionic NaCl crystal lattice. Distractor 1 = NaOH (Na + H₂O reaction). Distractor 3 = NaClO₃ (made by electrolysis of NaCl). Distractor 4 = NaClO (active ingredient in liquid bleach).

questions.stem: FLAME TEST: Lithium imparts crimson red, sodium imparts bright yellow, and POTASSIUM imparts a:

options.option_text: Blue green colour to the flame
Lilac (pale violet) colour to the flame
Brick red colour to the flame
Apple green colour to the flame

questions.explanation: Flame test colours: Li — CRIMSON RED. Na — bright YELLOW (sodium-D line, used in street lamps). K — LILAC / VIOLET (often viewed through cobalt blue glass to filter out Na contamination). Rb — red-violet. Cs — blue-violet. Ba — APPLE GREEN. Ca — BRICK RED. Cu — BLUE-GREEN. The colour comes from electrons returning from excited states; characteristic emission for each element.

questions.stem: Sodium and potassium are essential for human physiology because they:

options.option_text: Form bones and teeth structurally
Maintain electrolyte balance and nerve signals
Are major components of haemoglobin in blood
Form digestive enzymes inside the stomach lining

questions.explanation: Na⁺ and K⁺ — major electrolytes. Na/K-ATPase pump in cell membranes maintains the gradient (high K inside, high Na outside). This gradient drives nerve impulses (action potentials), muscle contraction, kidney function. Daily intake: Na ~1.5-2.3 g; K ~3.5-4.7 g. Imbalance → arrhythmias, weakness, cramps. Distractor 1 — Ca + P. Distractor 3 — Iron in haem. Distractor 4 — proteins / acids, not Na/K specifically.

questions.stem: LITHIUM is widely used today in:

options.option_text: Stainless steel manufacturing for kitchen pots
Rechargeable batteries for phones, laptops, and EVs
Bleaching agents in paper-mill processing plants
Solid rocket fuels for orbital launch vehicles

questions.explanation: Lithium-ion batteries — invented by Stanley Whittingham, John Goodenough, Akira Yoshino (Nobel 2019). High energy density per weight → revolutionised portable electronics + EVs. Lithium also used in lithium soap, ceramics, mood-stabiliser drugs (lithium carbonate for bipolar disorder). Major reserves — Australia, Chile (Salar de Atacama), Argentina, China; emerging in India (Reasi, J&K, ~5.9 Mt found 2023). Distractor 1 — stainless steel uses Cr, Ni. Distractor 3 = Cl-based. Distractor 4 = ammonium perchlorate / aluminium.
